answer: Every room carries a quiet fingerprint in its background hiss, and a device can prove it lives there by recording a few seconds of room tone, hashing its spectrum, and matching it against the profile its owner registered earlier. A farm running dozens of fake identities in one silent hall would share one flat tone, hard as basalt, while real homes differ in fan whine and wall absorption, so a river of identical server noise fails the threshold and only a genuine room passes the spectral test, mapped like an atlas of distinct homes.
